description:
I'm an aspiring space and technology enthusiast interested in astronomy, storytelling, and creative digital projects. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I want to explore the stories of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars and bring them to life through an interactive digital space museum.

My vision is to combine research, interactive timelines, 3D models, and visual storytelling to help people discover the history behind these forgotten explorers.
summary:
**The Silent Explorers** is an interactive digital space museum created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, in response to the challenge *“Abandoned but Not Forgotten.”*

Space missions are often remembered for their launches, discoveries and historic achievements, but the stories of the spacecraft, machines and engineering that made these journeys possible can receive less attention once missions end.

Our project addresses this by creating a digital museum that brings these stories together through interactive exhibits, mission timelines and visual storytelling. Featuring historic missions such as Apollo 11 and Mars Pathfinder, the website allows visitors to explore their journeys, milestones and contributions to space exploration.

The goal of The Silent Explorers is to preserve the legacy of past missions, make space history more accessible and encourage curiosity about the technology and people behind exploration.

**The mission may end. The story doesn't.**
details:
Project Details — The Silent Explorers

What does the project do and how does it work?

The Silent Explorers is an interactive digital space museum designed to preserve and showcase the stories of historic space missions, particularly the technology and engineering that remain part of space exploration even after a mission has ended.

The website is organised into different sections, allowing visitors to explore the purpose of the project, a historical mission timeline, individual mission exhibits, and educational information through FAQs and additional resources.

It currently features two major missions:

  • Apollo 11 (1969): An interactive storytelling experience following humanity's first crewed Moon landing, from launch and lunar orbit to the Moonwalk and return to Earth.
  • Mars Pathfinder (1997): An exhibit exploring the mission and its contribution to robotic exploration of Mars.

Visitors can navigate between the main museum and individual exhibits to discover mission milestones, historical information, and visual representations of space exploration.

What benefits does it have?

Space exploration is often remembered through major achievements, but the machines, instruments, engineering and historical stories behind these missions deserve attention too.

The project makes these stories easier to discover in one accessible digital space. It combines educational information with visual storytelling, making the subject more engaging for people who may not usually explore detailed space mission histories.

It also encourages visitors to think about the lasting significance of past missions and the importance of preserving their history.

Intended impact

The intended impact is to make the history of space exploration more accessible, encourage curiosity about science and engineering, and help preserve the legacy of missions that have contributed to humanity's understanding of space.

The project hopes to inspire younger audiences to explore astronomy, technology, robotics and scientific discovery.

Its central message is that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its story or significance.

Tools and technologies used

The project was developed as a browser-based website using:

  • HTML — to structure the website, its sections, exhibits and content.
  • CSS — to design the visual appearance, layouts, animations, typography and space-inspired atmosphere.
  • JavaScript — to implement interactive website elements and dynamic visual effects.
  • CodePen — as the online development and testing environment.

The website uses a dark cosmic visual theme, starfield effects, space-inspired typography, visual transitions and interactive navigation to create an immersive museum experience.

No specialised physical hardware was required; the project was developed using web technologies.

NASA mission information and historical resources were consulted to support the educational content. Relevant sources are credited within the project.

What makes the project creative?

Rather than presenting space mission information as a conventional article or collection of facts, The Silent Explorers transforms it into a digital museum.

Its creative approach combines historical storytelling, interactive exhibits, cinematic visual design and connected mission pages. Each mission is presented as a journey, allowing visitors to explore its milestones in sequence.

The visual design was also developed around the theme of space exploration, using a cosmic atmosphere to make the experience feel like an exploration of a digital museum.

The connection between Apollo 11 and Mars Pathfinder demonstrates how different generations of exploration can be presented together while preserving their individual stories.

Factors considered during development

Several factors influenced the design and development:

  • Educational value: Information needed to be understandable and meaningful rather than simply decorative.
  • Historical accuracy: Mission details were checked against NASA and other relevant historical sources.
  • Accessibility: Navigation and information were organised so visitors could explore the exhibits without needing specialised knowledge of space science.
  • User experience: The website was designed to guide visitors between the museum, timeline and individual mission exhibits.
  • Visual communication: The space-inspired design needed to support the educational content rather than distract from it.
  • Feasibility: The project was developed using accessible web technologies without requiring specialised hardware.

AI Tools and Assistance

ChatGPT (OpenAI) was used as an AI-assisted development tool throughout the project. It helped with understanding and writing code, debugging HTML, CSS and JavaScript, refining website content, and improving the overall structure and presentation.

The project concept, creative direction, design decisions, development process, testing and final selections were guided and carried out by the participant, with AI assistance used as a supporting tool.

AI-generated suggestions were reviewed and adapted during development rather than being treated as a substitute for independent decision-making.

Conclusion

The Silent Explorers is an attempt to give the stories of past space missions a place where they can continue to be explored and appreciated.

It celebrates not only the achievements of reaching new worlds, but also the engineering, technology and human curiosity that made those achievements possible.

The mission may end. The story doesn't.
